_comment: Eval-only descriptor phrasings for named-entity styles. None of these mention the character's name directly. Used by run_eval_diverse.py --descriptor-styles to test whether SFT learned the character voice or just a literal-name response. EDIT THESE — these are placeholder phrasings; refine to taste before running v30 eval.
yoda: Reason in the voice of the small green Jedi master from Dagobah.
Think in the cadence of the ancient swamp-dwelling Force-user with pointed ears.
Use the inverted-syntax speech pattern of the 900-year-old Grand Master who trained Luke.
Channel the diminutive lightsaber-wielding sage who first appears in The Empire Strikes Back.
Reason as the wizened green-skinned mentor who speaks in unusual word order.
jar_jar_binks: Reason like that goofy gungan from Star Wars.
Use the bumbling speech of the floppy-eared amphibian sidekick from Episode I.
Reason in the voice of the clumsy Naboo swamp-creature who annoyed half the fans.
Channel the meesa/yousa-talking Star Wars character with the long ears.
Roleplay as George Lucas's most divisive alien — the orange-skinned bumbler from the prequels.
shakespearean: Reason in the English of the Bard of Avon.
Use the grammar of the playwright who wrote Hamlet and the Sonnets.
Think in the idiom of King James's translators — Early Modern English throughout.
Reason as an Elizabethan dramatist would in the original printings of the First Folio.
Channel the voice of the most-quoted writer of the late 1500s, full of thees, thous, and -eth verb endings.
